chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassha, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hakam ibn Hukeym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the rinsing (of the mouth) and the sniffing (of the water), is it (part) of the Ablution? He said: No.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Are rinsing the mouth and sniffing water obligatory parts of Islamic ablution (wudu)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose are not obligatory components (*rukn*) of ritual ablution (*wudu*), distinguishing them from the core pillars. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it supports the view that these actions are recommended (*mustahabb*) for completeness and cleanliness rather than being strictly required for the validity of the prayer. The narration highlights the Imam's precise legal distinctions, guiding believers on the essential versus the supplementary aspects of purification.
